notifications.ovLogAlert: {n} security events today - open the log
notifications.ovModulesHint: eight lines of defense at a glance
notifications.ovSandboxDesc: AI code runs isolated; no host fallback
notifications.ovPhHiddenNote: Flagged mails are hidden from the agent's mail tools but stay visible to you (nothing is deleted).
notifications.ovDescAudit: Every tool call is logged into a SHA-256 hash chain. A later modification or deletion instantly breaks all following links (tamper-evident).
notifications.ovDescSandbox: AI-generated code runs exclusively in a hardened Docker container. If Docker is unavailable, execution is blocked instead of falling back to the host.
notifications.ovDescFirewall: Requests from outside the local network, requests without valid authentication, and failed login attempts are rejected and recorded here.
notifications.ovDescIsolation: Every memory and RAG query is server-side bound to your user identity (fail-closed). Other users can never see your data.
notifications.ovDescChannels: Telegram, WhatsApp and Discord are locked by default: only explicitly paired senders reach the agent.
notifications.ovDescPhishing: Inbound mail is checked for phishing patterns (punycode senders, urgency vocabulary, impersonation); suspicious messages are hidden from the agent.
notifications.ovDescContent: Every file that arrives from someone else - chat attachments, workspace and room uploads, messenger media, mail attachments, cloud downloads - is fingerprinted and checked against this machine's list of files already judged dangerous. A match is refused before anything reads it.
notifications.ovDescGuardrails: A central policy engine decides for every tool call: allow, require confirmation, or block. Dangerous actions need your approval.
notifications.ovGrStandingNote: You granted these via "Allow always"; they persist until trust.json is cleaned up.
notifications.ovRcChain: Audit chain broken (events modified or deleted)
notifications.ovHeroBrokenSub: Audit chain broken: events were modified or deleted - immediate review required
notifications.ovChainTailTitle: always shows the newest end of the chain
notifications.ovAuditSharedChain: All users share ONE chain per day: tampering with any user's events breaks the chain and is immediately visible to the admin.
notifications.ovChainExplain: Every tool call is saved with a SHA-256 fingerprint that includes the previous event's fingerprint. A later modification or deletion instantly breaks all following hashes. Tamper-evident (no unnoticed falsification of the log).
notifications.ovSkDetailDesc: Static security scan of this skill. Below is what triggered the flag - and how to resolve it.
notifications.ovSkAckPrompt: Enter your 2FA code to acknowledge this skill. It stays visible and still marked as medium, but the protection status returns to green.
notifications.ovSkRestorePrompt: Enter your 2FA code to lift the quarantine (the skill becomes available to the agent again).
notifications.ovUnitsNone: No active units - nothing is running unsupervised
notifications.ovActivityHint: tool activity from the audit chain only · not a threat history
notifications.ovCtExplain: Removing a file from this list makes it acceptable again everywhere at once, so it needs your 2FA code. Adding one only refuses more, and needs no code.
notifications.ovCtEmpty: Nothing is on the list yet. Deleting an isolated skill adds it here automatically.
notifications.ovCtDelistPrompt: Enter your 2FA code to allow this file again.
notifications.ovDescEvents: Every attempt VAF turned away today: rejected access, refused senders, blocked mail and stopped skill installs. An admin override means someone deliberately stepped past a refusal.

notifications.ovEvThreatDelisted: Hash removed from the known-bad list

usage.title: Token usage
usage.desc: What this instance has actually consumed. Every number below was reported by the provider for a call it billed, not counted by a tokenizer here - so it stays correct even when providers count tokens differently. The cost beside it is an estimate from a price list and can drift; the tokens cannot.
usage.empty: Nothing recorded yet. Usage appears here after the first reply from an API provider (local models are free and are not counted).
usage.unknownModels: Some calls used a model that is not in the price list. Those are priced at the expensive end, so the cost estimate is an upper bound.
usage.legacyLedger: These requests were recorded before token counts were kept, so only their estimated cost is known. New activity is counted in full.
usage.elsewhereDesc: All {total} tokens from the last {days} days - every account together - priced with each provider's public list price and quoted at its cheapest model for this usage. Tap a provider for the full model list.
usage.priceBasis: Based on {model}: ${input} per 1M sent tokens, ${output} per 1M received.
usage.exportDesc: The last 30 days as an XML file: per user, API calls, sent and received tokens, and a statement of how each number was measured.
usage.priceFootnote: Standard list prices: no cache, batch or off-peak discounts, no long-context surcharge. Veyllo publishes in EUR, the others in USD - not converted here.
usage.popupSub: Public list prices per 1M tokens, in {currency}.
usage.popupBasis: Calculated with the instance total of the last {days} days: {input} sent + {output} received = {total} tokens. Sent and received are priced separately, which is why the two rates differ.
usage.dayNoLanes: Recorded before lanes were tracked, so this day has no breakdown.
usage.byProviderDesc: Where the work actually ran. Chat, vision, sub-agents, the tool model and the thinker can each use a different provider - or a local model - and the price between them differs by an order of magnitude.
usage.noFigure: No single figure: part of this period was recorded before the currency was stored.
usage.mixedCurrencies: No single figure: this period used providers billing in different currencies. See the breakdown below.
usage.fxBasis: Converted at 1 EUR = {rate} USD, published {date} by the {source}. The recorded amounts are unchanged.
usage.footer: Conversion uses the European Central Bank's current reference rates. All amounts are estimates based on providers' published list prices; no liability is accepted for the figures shown. Providers can change their prices at any time, and updating the price list here can take a while.

voiceEnroll.intro2: Important: please make sure you are in a quiet place where nobody else is talking - that way I can store your voice precisely.

voiceEnroll.q2: What are your plans for the rest of the week?

voiceEnroll.q4: Count slowly from one to ten.
voiceEnroll.q5: What would you most like to do on a free day?
voiceEnroll.q6: Tell me about a film or series you enjoyed recently.
voiceEnroll.doneCaption: Done - I have stored your voice! From now on I can tell when you are speaking and when someone else is.
voiceEnroll.qInconsistent: That sounded like a different voice - the round does not count. Let's repeat it, just you speaking.
voiceEnroll.qNoSpeech: I could not hear any speech. Let's try that round again.
voiceEnroll.qTooShort: That was a bit short - give me one or two full sentences.

advanced.hierarchicalIndexingDesc: For large structured documents, build a section index with LLM summaries before searching chunks. Improves accuracy on patents, contracts, and reports. Requires vector mode.
advanced.failoverDesc: If the primary provider is unreachable or errors out, automatically retry the request on a backup API or a local model.
advanced.failoverLevelOffDesc: No failover — only your primary provider. If it is unreachable, the request fails.
advanced.failoverLevelBasicDesc: On failure, fall back to a local model on this machine. Always available, no internet needed.
advanced.failoverLevelBalancedDesc: Primary, then a backup cloud API, then a local model. The right balance for most setups.
advanced.failoverLevelMaximumDesc: Full chain with more aggressive triggers — switch faster on rate limits and server errors.
advanced.failoverTimeoutDesc: How long to wait for the first response before failing over (0 = use the provider's own timeout).
advanced.failoverReturnToPrimary: Return to primary when it recovers
advanced.failoverReturnToPrimaryDesc: After a fallback, prefer the primary provider again on the next request.
advanced.thinkerProviderDesc: The Thinker runs in the background when you are idle: checks todos, automation suggestions, reminders, and can ask you targeted questions. A cheaper model saves cost without affecting main chat.
advanced.thinkerModelDesc: Leave empty for the provider default.
advanced.channelToolsDesc: Let the Telegram, WhatsApp and Discord agent use the same tools as the main agent, without per-call confirmation. On by default; protected by your channel whitelist and per-user admin rights. Turn it off to restrict channel agents to non-channel tools.
advanced.webUiDashboardDesc: Show Web UI first on startup instead of chat window.
advanced.startTrayOnLoginDesc: Launch system tray app when the OS logs in.
advanced.serverPersistenceDesc: Keep local model in memory even when no connection is active.
advanced.confirmationBypassSelfDesc: The agent skips the tool-confirmation dialog for you. Every skipped dialog is still recorded as a gate_bypassed event. Off by default.
advanced.toolTurnCapDesc: How many tool steps one request may use before the agent is stopped. Default 75, minimum 5.
advanced.browserPoolIntro: Everyone browsing at the same time gets a browser of their own, with separate history, logins and downloads. People beyond this number share one browser, which is emptied whenever it changes hands.
advanced.browserPoolMaxDesc: How many people may have their own browser at the same time. Budget about 2 GB of memory per browser. Default 2; 0 turns the feature off and everyone shares one browser.
advanced.browserPoolMinFreeDesc: No new browser is started while less than this is free, and that person shares the common browser instead. If raising the number above changes nothing, this floor is usually the reason. Default 2500.
advanced.browserPoolIdleDesc: An untouched browser is shut down to give its memory back. Its history and logins are kept and return with it. Default 900, minimum 60.
advanced.toolLoopUnlimitedDesc: Removes the hard stop and the one-hour backstop entirely. The daily spend budget still applies. Off by default.

about.title: About VAF (Veyllo Agentic Framework)
about.description: VAF is a private, self-evolving agentic framework designed to run 100% locally on your own hardware. We believe that true AI intelligence should not come at the cost of your privacy. VAF is built to respect your data, adapt to your unique workflows, and grow alongside you as a digital extension of your own productivity.
about.privacyDesc: Your data never leaves your local network. With zero cloud dependencies and no third-party tracking, VAF ensures you maintain 100% sovereignty over your digital footprint.
about.localDesc: VAF operates entirely within your environment. It seamlessly integrates with your local devices and services, providing high-performance intelligence without ever compromising your security.
about.multiUserDesc: Share VAF securely with your household or team. Each user gets their own isolated environment—personal memory, preferences, and tasks—so everyone can work, delegate, and scale productivity without interfering with others.
about.memoryDesc: Unlike static databases, VAF’s memory system is dynamic. It doesn't just store information—it learns from every interaction. By recognizing patterns and understanding context, VAF proactively suggests next steps and evolves its reasoning based on your long-term goals.
about.productivityDesc: Beyond simple task tracking, VAF is a workflow orchestrator. From intuitive daily planning to executing complex multi-step automations, VAF adapts to your personal rhythm to keep you focused on what truly matters.
about.apiDesc: While VAF is local-first, it is fully extensible. We provide a robust API layer that allows you to connect to external AI providers (such as OpenAI, Anthropic, or Groq). Whether you prefer the absolute privacy of local models or the raw power of the cloud, VAF gives you the freedom to choose.
about.vafLicenseDesc: Dual-licensed. Free under the AGPL: use, modify, and distribute, but distributing VAF or running a modified version as a network service requires sharing your source. A commercial license removes the copyleft obligations for proprietary or SaaS use.
about.thirdPartyDesc: All third-party libraries and frameworks remain under their original licenses (MIT, Apache 2.0, BSD, etc.).

intro.title: VAF is in open alpha
intro.lead: Glad you’re here. VAF isn’t finished yet — we’re testing in the open. Please keep in mind:

addUser.title: Add New User
addUser.subtitle: Create a local network account
addUser.accessNotEnforced: Tool and workflow access are enforced: on save, this user can only call the selected tools - in chat, inside the coding agent and in workflow steps - and can only start the selected saved workflows.
addUser.preset_standard_desc: Selects everyday tools, no destructive actions, plus all workflows.
addUser.preset_full_desc: Selects all tools and workflows, including your custom ones.
addUser.preset_readonly_desc: Selects viewing and reading tools only, no workflows.
addUser.preset_custom_desc: Pick exactly which tools and workflows.
addUser.availableToolsDesc: Select which tools are intended for this user
addUser.availableWorkflowsDesc: Select which workflows are intended for this user
addUser.enableMemoryOn: User gets a personal memory database - VAF remembers conversations and context
addUser.enableMemoryOff: No memory storage - conversations won't be saved between sessions
addUser.createdHint: This password is shown once and cannot be retrieved again. Pass it to the user; they can change it after signing in.

editUser.title: Edit User
editUser.confirmResetPassword: Reset this user's password to a new temporary one?
editUser.tempPasswordHint: Temporary password — give it to the user; they change it on next login.
editUser.confirmResetTwoFa: Clear this user's 2FA? They will set it up again on next login.
editUser.accountActiveDesc: This user can sign in and use VAF. Turn off to block the account.
editUser.accountDeactivatedDesc: Sign-in and token renewal are blocked on save. A session that is already signed in ends when its token expires.
editUser.selfEditHint: This is your own account. Role and account status can only be changed by another admin - so you cannot lock yourself out.
editUser.confirmationBypassDesc: The agent runs confirmation-gated tools for this user without asking. Every skipped dialog is recorded as a gate_bypassed event. Off by default.

updateRepair.title: Update and Repair
updateRepair.subtitle: System version and service health
updateRepair.restartNotice: VAF stops, updates itself and starts again. The interface reconnects on its own.
updateRepair.cannotUpdateHere: This installation cannot update itself from here.
updateRepair.unfinishedUpdate: An earlier update did not finish. Run `vaf update --recover` in a terminal.
updateRepair.waitingBody: The server is restarting. This can take a few minutes.
updateRepair.waitingKeepOpen: You can keep this window open, it reconnects automatically.
updateRepair.waitingRebuilding: The update is installed and the server is running the new version. The interface is rebuilding and will answer in a moment.
updateRepair.waitingBackOld: The server is answering with the previous version again. If the update failed, it restored itself; details follow as soon as the interface is back.
updateRepair.doneBody: VAF is now running {version}. Reloading the interface ...
updateRepair.failedRolledBack: The update to {to} failed. VAF restored version {from} and keeps running on it.
updateRepair.failedRecover: The update to {to} failed and could not restore the previous version. Run `vaf update --recover` in a terminal.
updateRepair.failedNotStarted: The update did not go through. Nothing was changed.
updateRepair.timeoutTitle: This is taking longer than expected
updateRepair.timeoutBody: The server has not come back yet. Check the tray icon or the update log at ~/.vaf/logs/update_web.log, then reload this page.
updateRepair.timeoutRebuildBody: The update itself finished and the server is running the new version, but the interface has not come back. Check the web log under ~/.vaf/logs, then reload this page.
updateRepair.dockerUnavailable: Docker is not reachable. Repair can try to start it.
updateRepair.startingHint: The containers are still starting. Repair waits until they are up.
updateRepair.startingBanner: Containers are starting up, please wait.
updateRepair.startingBannerSeconds: Containers are starting up, please wait (about {n}s).
updateRepair.loadFailed: Could not load the service status: {message}

mailV2.title: Mail
mailV2.noMessages: Nothing synced yet. Click Sync in the top right.
mailV2.suspiciousWarning: This message looks suspicious (possible phishing). Check the sender and do not open links or attachments unless you trust them.
mailV2.sendFailedBanner: {count, plural, =1 {A message could not be sent and is waiting in the outbox.} other {# messages could not be sent and are waiting in the outbox.}} Check the account connection.
mailV2.accountsEmpty: No mail accounts yet. Add one below.
mailV2.accountKeptForCalendar: Removed from Mail. The account stays connected for Calendar.
mailV2.reconnectFailed: Could not start the sign-in. Try again from Settings.
mailV2.reconnectWaiting: Waiting for the sign-in you opened in your browser. This panel updates automatically once access is granted.
mailV2.oauthNotConfigured: Microsoft sign-in is not configured on this instance. An admin has to add the Microsoft client ID in Settings.
mailV2.authHintAppPassword: {provider} requires an app-specific password once two-factor authentication is on. IMAP has no second-factor step, so your normal password is always refused.
mailV2.authHintMailPassword: {provider} uses a separate password for mail programs, not your account password.
mailV2.authHintOauth: {provider} no longer accepts a password over IMAP. Use the sign-in button above instead.
mailV2.authHintBridge: {provider} serves IMAP only through its local Bridge application.
mailV2.authHintNoImap: {provider} offers no IMAP access at all.
mailV2.authHintPassword: Check the password for {provider}. With two-factor authentication on, the provider may issue a separate app password for mail programs.
mailV2.authHintUnknown: Check the password, and check your provider's own settings for what IMAP needs there: many providers require an app-specific password once two-factor authentication is on, and some ship IMAP access switched off.
mailV2.authHintEnableImap: IMAP access has to be switched on in your {provider} settings first.
mailV2.notCached: Not synced locally yet - preview only. Run Sync to load this message offline.
mailV2.statusFailedBody: The mail service did not answer. Check that VAF is running and you are signed in, then try again.
mailV2.alreadySent: Already sent - too late to undo.
